description:
A well established and growing Sheffield based business is looking to appoint an experienced Part time Finance Manager to take ownership of its finance function and provide clear, commercially focussed financial insight to the senior management team.

This is a genuinely broad role for someone who enjoys being close to the detail but can also step back and understand the bigger commercial picture. Reporting into the COO, you'll have ownership across the day-to-day finance function, while playing an important role in supporting the wider business as it continues to develop and grow.

The role

You'll take responsibility for the preparation of monthly management accounts, budgeting, forecasting and cash flow, alongside maintaining strong financial controls across the business.

There is also a strong commercial element to the position. You'll work closely with the CEO, COO and senior managers, providing analysis around profitability, margins, costs and performance, as well as helping the wider business understand the financial impact of operational and commercial decisions.

The role will also oversee transactional finance activity, including purchase and sales ledger, credit control, bank reconciliations and balance sheet controls, alongside responsibility for VAT, year-end accounts and liaison with external accountants and advisers.

As the business continues to develop existing services and explore new opportunities, you'll also have the opportunity to support financial modelling, business cases, new contracts and investment decisions.

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone with strong management accounting or financial management experience who is comfortable taking ownership rather than simply producing accounts.

ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent would be desirable, although suitably experienced qualified-by-experience candidates will also be considered.

Most importantly, you'll be commercially minded, hands-on and confident communicating financial information to non-finance stakeholders.

Why consider it?

The attraction of this role is the level of ownership and influence it offers, alongside the flexibility of a part-time position.

You'll have genuine visibility across the business, working closely with senior management and having the opportunity to shape the quality of financial information, processes and controls as the Group continues to evolve.

For an experienced Finance Manager looking for a part-time opportunity where they can make a tangible difference, this offers considerably more scope than a traditional part-time finance position.

description:
Sales Advisors

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

You'll join a lively sales team in our Doncaster contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.

FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.

GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

description:
About Us

Haywood & Padgett Ltd is an established food manufacturing business based in Barnsley, producing high-quality bakery products for customers across the UK.

Our people are at the heart of our business. As we continue to develop, we are looking for a Training Coordinator with food manufacturing experience to help ensure our employees have the skills, knowledge and confidence to do their jobs safely, effectively and to the required standards.

This is an exciting opportunity to take ownership of training across our site, working closely with managers and teams throughout the business to improve skills, support development and maintain high standards.

Role

Reporting to the HR Manager, you will coordinate and deliver training across our manufacturing operation, covering areas such as food safety, quality, health and safety, operational procedures and employee development.

You will spend time on the shop floor, working directly with employees and managers to identify training needs, deliver practical training and ensure employees understand and can confidently carry out their roles.

We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people, takes a hands-on approach and can help build a consistent and effective training programme across the business.

Key Responsibilities:

Coordinate and deliver training across production, hygiene, technical, warehouse and other departments.

Identify training needs and maintain training plans, training matrices and skills records.

Deliver practical training on food safety, hygiene, metal detection, coding and labelling, sieving, quality standards and other relevant manufacturing procedures.

Assess employees' understanding and practical competence, ensuring they are confident and capable before being signed off.

Work with managers and team leaders to identify skills gaps and ensure training is completed on time.

Coordinate refresher training and maintain accurate training and competency records.

Manage the company's online training platform, including course allocation, completion monitoring and reporting.

Develop clear and engaging training materials, including presentations, visual guides, toolbox talks and practical demonstrations.

Review training requirements following changes to processes, equipment, procedures, incidents or audit findings.

Support employee development, skills progression and opportunities for internal promotion.

Help improve the company's induction, training and development processes to ensure a consistent approach across all shifts.

Ensure training records are accurate, up to date and ready for customer, certification and internal audits.

Essential Qualifications and Experience

Previous experience working in food manufacturing is essential.

Experience delivering workplace training, coaching colleagues or coordinating training within a manufacturing environment.

A good understanding of food safety, hygiene, quality standards and health and safety within food production.

The ability to explain procedures clearly and deliver practical, engaging training.

Experience maintaining training records, skills matrices or competency assessments.

Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple training requirements and deadlines.

Confident communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships with employees and managers.

Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and the ability to maintain accurate records.

Flexibility to work across different shifts when required to support training needs.

Desirable Qualifications

A recognised Train the Trainer qualification.

Level 3 Award in Education and Training or an equivalent training qualification.

Level 3 Food Safety in Manufacturing.

Level 3 HACCP or equivalent.

Experience using an online learning or training management system.

Experience supporting employee development or training new starters.

We are happy to consider candidates who have the right food manufacturing and practical training experience but do not hold all the qualifications listed.

The Person

Approachable, enthusiastic and passionate about helping people learn.

Confident delivering practical training in a busy manufacturing environment.

A clear communicator who can adapt their approach to different employees and learning needs.

Comfortable working closely with production teams, managers and other departments.

Proactive in identifying opportunities to improve training and employee performance.

Professional and discreet when handling confidential employee information.

Confidentiality is essential. As part of the HR function, you will have access to sensitive employee and business information.

The postholder will provide a welcoming and inclusive volunteer journey, from recruitment and safer onboarding through induction, placement, ongoing support, development, recognition and, where appropriate, the ending of a volunteering arrangement.

Working closely with managers and teams, the Volunteer Coordinator will help ensure volunteers are appropriately matched, supported and valued, and that volunteering activity is safe, effective and aligned with the mission and values of Rotherham Hospice.

Key Responsibilities

Volunteer recruitment and onboarding:
- Support the Volunteer Manager in creating clear, meaningful and accessible volunteer role descriptions.
- Assist the Volunteer Manager in promoting opportunities through appropriate community networks, digital channels and local partnerships to attract a diverse range of volunteers.
- Coordinate enquiries, applications, informal interviews, references, DBS checks where appropriate, and other safer recruitment checks.
- Maintain accurate records of volunteers on the Hospice Volunteer system, Volunteero
- Assist management in matching volunteers to suitable roles, considering their skills, interests, availability, support needs and the requirements of the Hospice.
- Coordinate volunteer agreements, induction, mandatory training and introductory or shadowing arrangements.

Volunteer support, engagement and recognition:
- Act as an approachable first point of contact for volunteers.
- Assist manager in ensuring volunteers receive appropriate day-to-day direction, supervision and wellbeing support.
- Assist in providing advice to manager on responding to concerns, attendance issues or difficulties promptly, fairly and sensitively, escalating safeguarding, conduct or other significant matters in line with Hospice procedures.
- Help in develop opportunities for training, progression and wider involvement, and coordinate activities that thank and recognise volunteers for their contribution.
- Support positive endings to volunteering arrangements, including exit feedback where appropriate

Administration, compliance and reporting:
- Maintain accurate and confidential volunteer records, including applications, checks, training, placements, attendance and contact details using the Volunteer Information System
- Maintain accurate data relating to volunteer numbers, vacancies, retention, training completion and contribution, producing reports and insights to support planning and demonstrate impact.
- Assist in ensuring volunteering activity follows relevant Hospice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, confidentiality, equality, health and safety, data protection and volunteer expenses.
- Support role risk assessments and ensure volunteers understand how to raise concerns and work safely within the boundaries of their role.

Volunteer programme development:
- Promote an inclusive, accessible and positive volunteering culture that reflects the Hospice values.
- Maintain and help develop links with local volunteer organisations, community groups, education providers and other partners.
- Contribute to the review and improvement of volunteer policies, procedures, systems and the overall volunteer experience
